Pricing.faq1Q: What is the affordable AI model API at 9inference?
Pricing.faq1A: 9inference is an affordable, pay-per-token AI model API gateway. You access DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Kimi and other models through a single OpenAI-compatible API key, with token pricing in rupiah and no mandatory subscription.
Pricing.faq2Q: What is TOKS and how does its pricing work?
Pricing.faq2A: TOKS is our internal credit unit. 1 TOKS = Rp1,000 = US$0.0553. Each model has a rate per 1 million tokens in rupiah; you only pay for tokens actually used. No subscription, no minimum.
Pricing.faq3Q: What's the difference between PAYG and Packages?
Pricing.faq3A: PAYG: you top up your TOKS balance and it's deducted per token actually used — the balance never expires and works across all models. Packages: you pay once for a quota of millions of tokens with a dedicated API key active for 24 hours — ideal for heavy workloads at a fixed price. Package quota does not use your PAYG balance, and vice versa.
Pricing.faq4Q: Do I need a credit card to start?
Pricing.faq4A: No. Sign up free, create an API key, and top up anytime. You can start with any amount — there's no minimum deposit.
Pricing.faq5Q: What happens if my credit runs out?
Pricing.faq5A: Requests return a top-up reminder instead of failing silently. Add credit in your wallet and you're back online within seconds. Your API key and settings stay intact.
Pricing.faq6Q: Are there hidden fees or subscriptions?
Pricing.faq6A: None. You only pay for tokens used at the published rates. No monthly fees, no platform fees, no per-seat fees. The price you see is the price you pay.
Pricing.faq7Q: Can I switch models without changing my code?
Pricing.faq7A: Yes. 9inference is OpenAI-compatible — change the model parameter in your request and your SDK stays the same. Switch between GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi and more with a single line.
Pricing.faq8Q: Are my data and API keys secure?
Pricing.faq8A: API keys are hashed at rest, credentials are encrypted, and per-key rate limits prevent abuse. We never train models on your data and never share your prompts with third parties.
Pricing.faq9Q: Is there a refund for unused credit?
Pricing.faq9A: Unused credit never expires. If within 14 days of your first top-up you feel 9inference isn't a fit, contact support for a full refund of your remaining balance.

Docs.title: API Documentation
Docs.subtitle: 9inference exposes an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API. Point your existing SDK at our base URL and start inferencing in minutes.
Docs.step1Desc: Head to API Keys and generate a production key. It follows the sk_live_… format.
Docs.step3Desc: Any OpenAI-compatible client works — just swap the base URL.
Docs.authenticationDesc: Send your API key as a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
Docs.billingDesc: Every response includes an x_billing header with token usage and the deducted cost. You only pay for tokens consumed.
Docs.packageModelsDesc: Models available through the package endpoint. The ones enabled for your key depend on the package you bought.
Docs.endpointsDesc: 9inference has two different base URLs depending on your API key type. Make sure you use the matching one — this is the most common cause of IDE setup errors.
Docs.paygDesc: Your balance is charged for the tokens you use.
Docs.paygKey: Use a regular API key from <link>API Keys</link>.
Docs.paygBilling: Billed from your account balance, per token.
Docs.packageDesc: A fixed token quota from the package you bought.
Docs.packageKey: Use the package API key from <link>Packages</link>.
Docs.packageBilling: Deducts from the package token quota, not your balance.
Docs.endpointsWarning: Keys and URLs are not interchangeable. A package API key on the PAYG URL is rejected with 403 package_endpoint_required, and a PAYG API key on the package URL is rejected with 403 package_key_required.
Docs.opencodeIntro: OpenCode is a terminal-based coding agent that is fully compatible with 9inference. Follow these steps to connect it — the only difference between PAYG and package is the base URL and the API key.
Docs.opencodeStep1Desc: Requires Node.js. Other install methods (script, Homebrew, etc.) are on <link>opencode.ai</link>.
Docs.opencodeStep2Title: Store your API key as an environment variable
Docs.opencodeStep2Desc: Replace sk_live_xxx with your API key (PAYG or package). This keeps the key out of the config file.
Docs.opencodeStep3Desc: Save it in your project root as opencode.json, or at ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json to apply it to every project. Pick the config that matches your API key type.
Docs.opencodeConfigNote: Add more models under models using the exact IDs from the model lists below. The model field sets the default model in provider/model-id format.
Docs.opencodeStep4Title: Run it and pick a model
Docs.opencodeStep4Desc: Open a terminal in your project folder, run opencode, then type /models to pick a 9inference model.
Docs.harnessIntro: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) is the open-source agent harness from DeepSeek with a local Web UI. 9inference is added as a "Custom model API" — the only difference between PAYG and package is the base URL and the API key.
Docs.harnessStep1Desc: Requires Node.js. This command opens the Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080.
Docs.harnessStep2Title: Add 9inference as a Custom model API
Docs.harnessStep2Desc: Open Settings → Models, choose Add model provider, then switch to Custom model API. Fill in the form for your API key type:
Docs.harnessStep3Title: Fetch the model list and pick a model
Docs.harnessStep3Desc: Under Model catalog, click Fetch available models, tick the models you want, then Add selected and save. If the list does not load, type the model IDs by hand using the model lists below. The 9inference models then appear in the model picker and work without a restart.
Docs.harnessAdvancedDesc: The form above writes to ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml. You can also edit that file directly; keep the API key in the NINEINFERENCE_API_KEY environment variable.
Docs.harnessAdvancedNote: The compat block makes Harness send requests in the standard OpenAI shape (max_tokens, no developer role). Add it if every request is rejected even though the key and URL are right. If the file already has other providers under llm-pi-ai, merge them — do not overwrite the whole block.
Docs.opencodeErrPackageEndpoint: You are using a package API key on the PAYG URL. Change baseURL to https://9inference.cloud/v1/package.
Docs.opencodeErrPackageKey: You are using a PAYG API key on the package URL. Change baseURL to https://9inference.cloud/v1.
Docs.opencodeErrQuota: Your package token quota is used up. Buy a new package or switch to PAYG.
Docs.opencodeErrAuth: The API key is wrong, disabled, or expired. Also check that the environment variable is loaded (open a new terminal).
Docs.opencodeErrExtraInputs: The tool is sending non-standard fields. Use one of the IDEs above with the provided config.
Docs.ideDesc: Pick the IDE or tool you use to see its setup steps.
Docs.harnessHint: Agent harness with a local Web UI
Docs.ninerouterHint: Local AI router for all your tools
Docs.ninerouterIntro: 9router is an open-source AI router that runs on your machine. Register 9inference once as an OpenAI Compatible provider, and Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, OpenCode, and other tools can use 9inference models through a single local endpoint — with key rotation and automatic fallback.
Docs.ninerouterKeysTitle: There are two different API keys
Docs.ninerouterKeysDesc: Your 9inference API key goes into 9router only (step 3). Your 9router API key goes into your AI tools (step 5). Mixing them up is the most common cause of 401 errors.
Docs.ninerouterStep1Desc: Requires Node.js (latest LTS recommended). Once running, open the dashboard at http://localhost:20128/dashboard. Keep the terminal open while you use 9router.
Docs.ninerouterStep1Note: The default login password is 123456. Change it right after your first login, especially if 9router is reachable from other devices.
Docs.ninerouterStep2Title: Add 9inference as an OpenAI Compatible provider
Docs.ninerouterStep2Desc: Open Providers, click Add OpenAI Compatible, and fill in the form for your API key type:
Docs.ninerouterStep2Note: The Prefix becomes the model name prefix in 9router, e.g. 9i/model-id. API Type must be Chat Completions — do not pick Responses API. The Base URL ends at /v1 or /v1/package, without /chat/completions.
Docs.ninerouterStep2Check: Optional: fill API Key (for Check) with your 9inference API key and Model ID (optional) with any model, then click Check to verify the connection before saving.
Docs.ninerouterStep2Both: Have both a PAYG and a package key? Add them as two separate providers with different prefixes — you can combine them into a Combo in step 6.
Docs.ninerouterStep3Desc: Click the new provider to open its detail page. Under Connections, click Add API Key and paste your 9inference API key. PAYG keys are on the API Keys page; package keys are on the Packages page.
Docs.ninerouterStep3Note: You can add more than one API key to the same provider. 9router can rotate between them automatically (Round Robin) to spread the load.
Docs.ninerouterStep4Desc: Still on the provider detail page, click Import from /models to pull every 9inference model automatically. To add models one by one, click Add Model and type the Model ID exactly as shown in the model list below.
Docs.ninerouterStep4Note: Once imported, call models using the prefix/model-id format:
Docs.ninerouterStep5Title: Create a 9router API key and connect your AI tools
Docs.ninerouterStep5Desc: Open Endpoint & Key, click Create Key, enter a Key Name (e.g. "Laptop"), then copy the key — it is shown only once. Then configure your AI tool like this:
Docs.ninerouterStep5Test: Test it from the terminal first. If the response contains the model's answer, 9router is connected to 9inference:
Docs.ninerouterStep5Tools: Tip: the CLI Tools menu in the 9router dashboard can write the config for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and other tools automatically — just pick a 9i/… model there.
Docs.ninerouterStep6Title: Optional: create a Combo with automatic fallback
Docs.ninerouterStep6Desc: Open Combo & Vision Adapter, click Create Combo, enter a Combo Name (letters, numbers, -, _ and . only), add models via Add Model, then pick the Fallback — try in order strategy. Order models from highest priority.
Docs.ninerouterStep6Example: The example above uses the package first. When the package quota runs out or a request fails, 9router automatically switches to PAYG. In your AI tool, just set the model to the combo name: 9inference-hemat.
Docs.ninerouterErr401: The tool is using your 9inference API key instead of the 9router API key from Endpoint & Key. Also make sure that key is not paused.
Docs.ninerouterErrModel: The model name is missing its prefix. Use 9i/model-id (or 9i-paket/model-id), not just model-id.
Docs.ninerouterErrImportTitle: Import from /models is empty or fails
Docs.ninerouterErrImport: No API key has been added under Connections yet, or the key type does not match the Base URL. Package keys must use https://9inference.cloud/v1/package.
Docs.ninerouterErrPackage: The API key and Base URL on the 9router provider are mismatched. Edit the provider and match the Base URL to the key type.
Docs.ninerouterErrApiTypeTitle: Every request fails even though the key is correct
Docs.ninerouterErrApiType: The provider's API Type is set to Responses API. Edit the provider and switch it to Chat Completions.
Docs.ninerouterErrRefused: 9router is not running or its terminal was closed. Run the 9router command again and retry.
Docs.zedHint: Open-source code editor with a built-in AI agent
Docs.zedIntro: Zed is a fast, open-source (GPL) code editor written in Rust with a built-in Agent Panel. 9inference is added as an "OpenAI API Compatible" provider — the only difference between PAYG and package is the API URL and the API key.
Docs.zedStep1Desc: Download Zed for macOS, Linux, or Windows from <link>zed.dev/download</link>, then open the app.
Docs.zedStep2Desc: Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P), run zed: open settings file, and merge the following language_models block into your settings:
Docs.zedStep2Note: You can add both at once. The Provider ID determines the API key environment variable name. Without editing JSON: run agent: open settings, click Add Provider in the LLM Providers section, and fill in:
Docs.zedStep3Desc: Run agent: open settings, find the nineinference provider under LLM Providers, and paste your API key. Zed stores it in the system keychain, not in settings.json.
Docs.zedStep3Env: Or use an environment variable. Its name is the Provider ID in upper snake case plus _API_KEY. Restart Zed after setting it:
Docs.zedStep3Warning: Never put API keys in settings.json. A non-empty environment variable takes precedence over the keychain value.
Docs.zedStep4Desc: Open the Agent Panel (agent: toggle focus), click the model selector in the thread, and pick a model from nineinference or nineinference-paket. The selection is saved as agent.default_model.
Docs.zedStep4Image: The PAYG config in step 2 already sets "images": true for image-capable models. Do not enable it for other models — requests may fail when you attach an image.
Docs.zedErrNoProviderTitle: Provider does not show up in the model selector
Docs.zedErrNoProvider: Make sure settings.json is valid JSON and the language_models block is not duplicated, then check that the API key is set. Providers without a key cannot be used.
Docs.zedErrAuth: The API key is wrong, deleted, or the PAYG/package key is swapped with its provider. Re-enter the key via agent: open settings or check the environment variable.
Docs.zedErrTools: Some models do not support tool calling. Pick another model, or set "tools": false on that model to use it for plain chat.
Docs.opencodeImageDesc: By default OpenCode treats models from a custom provider as text-only. To send images, mark image-capable models with attachment and modalities under models in opencode.json:
Docs.opencodeImageConfigNote: The PAYG config in step 3 already includes these fields for image-capable models. Do not add them to models without image support — requests may fail when you attach an image. After changing the config, close and reopen OpenCode.
Docs.opencodeImageModelsEmpty: No PAYG model supports image input right now.
Docs.opencodeImagePackageNote: For package models, add the fields above only if that model actually supports images.
Docs.opencodeImageHowTitle: How to send images in OpenCode:
Docs.opencodeImageHowPaste: Paste from clipboard — take a screenshot, then press Ctrl+V in the OpenCode prompt. The image appears as an attachment; type your question and press Enter.
Docs.opencodeImageHowDrop: Drag & drop — drag an image file (PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF) from your file explorer into the terminal window. OpenCode turns the file path into an attachment automatically.
Docs.opencodeImageHowPath: Paste a file path — copy the image's full path (e.g. C:\Users\name\Desktop\error.png or ~/Desktop/error.png) and paste it into the prompt.
Docs.opencodeImageRunDesc: Without opening the TUI, use opencode run with the -f flag (repeat it for several images) and -m to pick an image-capable model:
Docs.opencodeImageRunPrompt: Explain the error in this screenshot
Docs.opencodeImageLimits: Size limits: up to 20 MB per attachment in the TUI and 10 MB per file for opencode run. If Ctrl+V only pastes text in your terminal, use drag & drop or paste the file path.
Docs.opencodeErrNoImage: The selected model is not marked as image-capable in opencode.json, so OpenCode does not send the image. Add attachment and modalities as in step 5, or pick a model that supports images.

Status.title: Service Status
Status.subtitle: Uptime and response duration for each model, measured from real requests to the 9inference API.
Status.overallOutage: Some models are experiencing an outage
Status.historyLabel: Uptime history for the last {days} days
Status.methodBody: Uptime is the share of successful requests versus requests that failed because of the service or its upstream. Requests rejected for an empty balance or quota, a model that is not allowed, or a malformed request do not count as downtime. Response duration is the total time until the response finishes, including streaming, so it depends on answer length. Status uses the last hour of data, or the last 24 hours when traffic is low.
